A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Graph Diffusion Network research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C. Retained content can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Schelling and Predator–Prey simulations, trained surrogate and ablation results, EMD and sMAPE evaluations, and spatial analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds GNN-only evaluations, scalability experiments, and an AR(1) forecasting comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed GDN architecture, ramification sampling, denoising objective, and generation procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. The GNN-only model is an added comparator, not a modification of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three Schelling tolerance regimes and four Predator–Prey transition regimes. The added scalability studies vary grid size, agent count, and training samples within the retained Predator–Prey task, without introducing another domain or task.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates one ablation, renamed diffusion-only in v2. V2 adds a deterministic GNN-only comparator to the main quantitative and trajectory comparisons, plus an AR(1) macro-forecasting baseline in Appendix C.5 and Figure 20.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings remain, but Appendix A.5 adds controlled sweeps over 50–500 ramifications and 2048–8192 agents, including a roughly constant-training-time tradeoff. New comparator protocols include MSE training with batch size 16 for GNN-only and separate least-squares AR(1) fits for macro variables.

E4.justification: V1 explicitly declines to evaluate diffusion removal; v2 performs that ablation and examines its spatial and temporal failures. Appendix A.5 additionally tests sensitivity to ramification count, scaling with agent count, and whether larger systems permit fewer ramifications at similar training cost.

E5.justification: V2 specifies ten runs for the ramification sweep and five for the agent-count and tradeoff studies, reporting means and standard-deviation error bars. The original eight-seed evaluations and 100 simulation rollouts remain unchanged; their replication count was not increased.

E6.justification: V2 adds GNN-only errors and failure patterns, AR(1) forecast trajectories, and scalability measurements. For example, its Table 2 reports EMD 0.0161 at 50 ramifications and 0.0088 at 500. The original plotted GDN/diffusion-only results and state-wise heatmap are retained; the additions do not establish improved same-setting GDN performance.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds the formal AR(1) recurrence and its Gaussian-noise assumption. The existing GDN equations, ABM definitions, and metric formulas remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claim: a differentiable graph-and-diffusion surrogate learns individual stochastic behavior and reproduces emergent dynamics beyond training. The additional experiments support this existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting larger agent populations to greater statistical coverage and fewer required ramifications, and attributes AR(1) failures to missing micro-level information. It also qualifies direct empirical application as requiring sufficient comparable agent-context observations. The original known-graph and complex-ABM limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new GNN-only architecture and training settings and the AR(1) fitting procedure. Appendix A.5 revises training time from 7–12 hours to about one hour and 25-step generation from 10–12 seconds to about 7.5 seconds, without explaining the difference. Hardware, original GDN settings, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds benchmark-justification references, including Jamali and Ten Broeke, and removes the Vaswani citation. Section 2 expands the distinction from Casert’s approach through its continuous-time and explicit-transition requirements. Core novelty positioning remains; relocated references and publication metadata updates are not new cited works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with targeted language, terminology, contact/header, and ablation-discussion edits. Appendix A.5 is reorganized, C.5 is added, and supplementary references are separated, without a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Main and appendix comparisons gain GNN-only panels or series, with revised axes, legends, and captions. V2 adds three scalability tables, three scalability figures, and the AR(1) comparison figure, and redraws Figure 1. Other appendix figures are matched retained displays despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important experimental gap by evaluating the diffusion-removal control that v1 dismissed. Together with controlled scalability studies, this substantially strengthens architectural validation and evidence about practical data and computational requirements. These gains remain substantial despite reporting problems: Figure 4 plots some new GNN-only sMAPE values above Equation 6’s upper bound of 2, and the large runtime revision is unexplained.
